Before launch, Linux host-native labview-cli runs read labview.conf (under ~/natinst/.config/LabVIEW-<version>/, ~/.config/natinst/LabVIEW-<version>/, or /etc/natinst/LabVIEW-<version>/) and block execution with linux-vi-server-tcp-disabled when server.tcp.enabled=False, when the key is absent, or when no candidate config is readable (NI Linux defaults VI Server TCP off); when requestedLabviewVersion is unset the year is inferred from the resolved labviewExe directory (e.g. LabVIEW-2026-64). The lvcompare engine is exempt from this preflight. When TCP is enabled the resolved server.tcp.port (default 3363) is passed to LabVIEWCLI as -PortNumber. Linux host-native staging mirrors VI inputs and report output under a short tmpdir (default $TMPDIR/vi-history-suite-runtime, overridable via LVIE_LINUX_RUNTIME_TMPDIR, opt-out via LVIE_LINUX_DISABLE_RUNTIME_TMPDIR=1) using a directory-boundary check so similarly-prefixed paths do not bypass the workaround for LabVIEW 2026 Linux path-table corruption.

Title: Reactive Runtime Provider Selection And Quick-Pick

Title: Concurrent LabVIEW Bitness Conflict Diagnostic
Notes: Windows host preflight infers running LabVIEW bitness from Get-Process executable path (Program Files vs Program Files (x86)) and propagates labviewProcessBitness/labviewProcessExecutablePath through RuntimeProcessObservation. comparisonRuntimeLocator.locate short-circuits to blockedReason=windows-host-bitness-conflict when observed bitness differs from selected; comparisonRuntimeDoctor emits a next-action naming both bitnesses and viHistorySuite.labviewBitness. classifyRuntimeFailure rewrites command-exited-nonzero to labview-host-bitness-conflict when exit-snapshot LabVIEW bitness mismatches. Title: LabVIEW CLI Prerequisite Gate For VI History Open

Title: LabVIEW CLI Install Offer When LabVIEW Is Installed

Title: Windows Host-Native VI Server TCP Preflight Parity
Notes: Before launching LabVIEWCLI, Windows host-native labview-cli runs read the LabVIEW.ini adjacent to the selected LabVIEW executable and block execution with blockedReason='windows-vi-server-tcp-disabled' when server.tcp.enabled=False is explicitly set, mirroring the Linux labview.conf preflight from VHS-REQ-156. The WindowsLabviewTcpSettings interface exposes a tri-state viServerTcpEnabled (true when enabled or absent — Windows defaults VI Server TCP on; false only on explicit False; 'unknown' when the ini is not readable). The block runs after preflightLinuxHostRuntimeSurface and before preflightWindowsHostRuntimeSurface, so the explicit ini-disabled signal wins over the bitness-conflict surface arm covered by VHS-REQ-621. The lvcompare engine is exempt because it does not connect to LabVIEW VI Server. The preflight does not auto-mutate LabVIEW.ini — write actions race with running LabVIEW IDE rewrites on clean shutdown. The vihs --validate runtime-validation proof serializes the observed host VI Server port (runtime.hostLabviewTcpPort) and its LabVIEW.ini path (runtime.hostLabviewIniPath) so real-hardware evidence proves a non-default server.tcp.port was admitted without a false conflict; the Windows runtime matrix harness port-A scenario derives its expected VI Server port from the selected install's own LabVIEW.ini (the same parse the product uses) rather than a hardcoded or operator-supplied constant, then asserts the admitted run's proof reports hostLabviewIniPath equal to that selected install's ini and hostLabviewTcpPort equal to the port parsed from it — keeping the contract correct for whatever port the operator configures and proving the product read the selected install rather than the latest-used one.

Title: Actionable VI Server Disabled Comparison Guidance
Notes: When a comparison is blocked with windows-vi-server-tcp-disabled or linux-vi-server-tcp-disabled (from the VHS-REQ-623 / VHS-REQ-156 preflights), deriveRuntimeDoctorNextAction emits a VI-Server-specific next-action that names enabling VI Server in LabVIEW (Tools → Options → VI Server) or setting server.tcp.enabled=True (LabVIEW.ini on Windows, labview.conf on Linux), then restarting LabVIEW and rerunning report generation. The next-action becomes the doctor summary's final line so the existing blocked-compare warning notification and history panel runtime result surface the same actionable guidance on both platforms. Detection stays in the compare-time preflights; this requirement owns only the user-facing next-action copy and does not add a pre-panel gate.

Title: Actionable VI Server Guidance For LabVIEW CLI Connection Failure
Notes: When a host-native LabVIEWCLI compare attempt fails with labview-cli-connection-failed (LabVIEWCLI exit error -350000), deriveRuntimeDoctorNextAction emits a VI-Server-specific failed-state next-action naming VI Server (TCP/IP) disabled for the selected LabVIEW as the most common cause and the enable path (Tools → Options → VI Server / server.tcp.enabled=True and the configured port), restart LabVIEW, then rerun. Complements VHS-REQ-628 for the post-attempt case the VHS-REQ-623/156 ini preflight cannot catch (absent key, unreadable ini, or written only on clean LabVIEW exit). The -350000 classification is unchanged; this requirement owns only the failed-state next-action copy.

Title: Pre-Panel VI Server Prerequisite Gate For VI History Open
Notes: labviewViHistory.open consults the selected host LabVIEW VI Server config after the Git and LabVIEW-CLI gates and refuses to open the panel with a warning toast naming VI Server and the enable path unless server.tcp.enabled=True is explicit. isViServerExplicitlyEnabledInConfig requires an explicit True (case/quote/whitespace tolerant); absent key, False, and unreadable count as not enabled. decideViServerOpenGate allows on not-ready detection, active Docker provider, no resolvable host installation, or non-host platforms; otherwise it reads the Windows LabVIEW.ini adjacent to the selected exe or the Linux labview.conf candidates (reusing the VHS-REQ-156 builder) and blocks unless one is explicitly enabled. Strict open-gate-only rule; the compare-time VHS-REQ-623/156 preflight is unchanged. No TCP port probe. Accepted tradeoff: false-positive block for Windows hosts running VI Server on without an explicit key.

Title: Host LabVIEW Install Catalog Parity
Notes: Activation-time runtime detection (VHS-REQ-616) and the comparison runtime locator (VHS-REQ-155) derive their documented host LabVIEW/LabVIEWCLI/LVCompare install locations from one shared catalog (src/tooling/labviewInstallCatalog.ts) so the lightweight detector recognizes every documented LabVIEW and LabVIEW CLI filesystem install location the locator recognizes, preventing the LabVIEW CLI open gate from false-blocking a host the compare engine can serve. Activation detection resolves the host LabVIEW executable and LabVIEW CLI; LVCompare is a locator-only surface fed by the same catalog. Catalog supplies the supported year range, Linux quarterly (LabVIEW-<year>Q1-64/Q3) plus plain install dirs and shared nilvcli launchers, Windows LabVIEW <year>[ Q1| Q3] folders, the canonical 32-bit shared Windows LabVIEW CLI path, and LVCompare paths. detectLinux/WindowsHostInstallations enumerate the catalog (a quarterly-only Linux host is now detected); buildDocumentedRuntimeCandidates derives the same scan, with the Windows registry query remaining the locator-only superset for non-default installs. Catalog is pure (no VS Code/fs/child-process) so tooling and reporting consume it without a cycle. Activation detection stays filesystem-only; registry-only/custom-path parity is tracked separately.

Title: Manual LabVIEW Runtime Path Override
Notes: viHistorySuite.labviewCliPath and viHistorySuite.labviewExePath let users override host LabVIEW discovery for installs auto-detection does not cover. package.json contributes both as strings and lists both in capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces.restrictedConfigurations (they name executables the comparison launches, so untrusted workspaces cannot supply them). readComparisonRuntimeSettings reads both (trimmed; blank -> undefined) into ComparisonRuntimeSettings, so locateComparisonRuntime builds configured candidates and returns configured-labview-cli-path-missing/configured-labview-exe-path-missing for a non-existent path. decideLabviewCliOpenGate allows labviewViHistory.open when a non-empty labviewCliPath is configured, trusting the override (gate stays pure/window-free, no stat); extension.ts passes the configured path. Existence validation stays with the compare-time locator, making the runtime doctor's pre-existing set-the-path guidance functional end to end.

Title: Authoritative Host Fallback For LabVIEW CLI Open Gate
Notes: When the synchronous LabVIEW CLI open gate (VHS-REQ-627) would block labviewViHistory.open from the filesystem-only activation detection (VHS-REQ-616), the open command consults a bounded on-demand authoritative probe before blocking so a Windows registry-resolved / custom-path LabVIEW install the detector cannot see (it never queries the registry) does not false-block. probeWindowsRegistryHostLabviewAvailable reuses the locator's shipped reg query plans+parser and returns true only when a registry-resolved LabVIEW.exe (named directly, or derived from the National Instruments install-directory Path value the stock NI registry actually records) exists on disk AND the shared Windows LabVIEW CLI exists on disk; it performs no container/process probes and never throws. decideLabviewCliOpenGateWithRegistryFallback returns the base decision unless it is block on Windows with a probe supplied, then allows when the probe reports available (fail-closed to the base block on throw). extension.ts awaits the fallback with the registry probe only on the block branch. The synchronous decideLabviewCliOpenGate contract (VHS-REQ-627/629/633) is unchanged; activation detection stays filesystem-only.

Matching-version sessions remain admitted; compare-time VHS-REQ-621 and VHS-REQ-155 are unchanged.

All other blocked and failed reasons keep their existing diagnostics surface.

Title: Docker Not Installed Comparison Toast
Notes: Sibling of VHS-REQ-642 for the Docker-not-installed case (dockerCliAvailable=false) under blockedReason docker-provider-unavailable/docker-only-provider-unavailable/auto-docker-installed-provider-unavailable: isDockerNotInstalledBlock returns true (mutually exclusive with the daemon-down predicate on dockerCliAvailable); the action returns outcome blocked-docker-not-installed and suppresses the report webview only when the packet archived (retainedArchiveAvailable!=false), falling through to open the webview directly when archiving failed so diagnostics are never lost. openViHistoryCommand shows a single platform-aware toast built by buildDockerNotInstalledMessage (Docker Desktop on win32, Docker otherwise) with Install Docker (opens INSTALL_DOCKER_URL via openExternal) and Show diagnostics (open retained packet) instead of the verbose runtime warning. No automatic install or process launch; link only. The VHS-REQ-642 daemon-down toast and all other blocked/failed reasons are unchanged.

The body is carried through ComparisonReportRevisionMetadata from the in-memory retained-history commits already passed to comparison generation (no new Git reads, no regression of VHS-REQ-008), rendered HTML-escaped with multi-line preserved (no regression of VHS-REQ-017). Undefined (not-retained) metadata renders the shared not-retained fallback; a retained empty/whitespace body (including the synthesized working-tree revision, VHS-REQ-641) renders a distinct empty-body fallback. Reuses the VHS-REQ-639 history-panel commit-body pattern; history-panel and review-packet body rendering and comparison runtime behavior are unchanged.

Title: Configurable Comparison Report Flags
Notes: The LabVIEW comparison report difference-suppression filters are user- and workspace-configurable through native VS Code settings under viHistorySuite.report.*: boolean filters ignoreViAttributes ignoreFrontPanel ignoreFrontPanelObjectPosition ignoreBlockDiagram and ignoreBlockDiagramCosmetic. readComparisonReportOptions reads them at the comparison-report action boundary and threads them through buildComparisonReportExecutionPlan into buildLabviewCliCreateComparisonReportPlan; each enabled filter emits exactly its verified LabVIEWCLI CreateComparisonReport flag (-noattr -nofp -nofppos -nobd -nobdcosm). The report output format is fixed to single-file HTML (-ReportType htmlsinglefile, hardcoded in the CLI plan) and is NOT configurable: there is no viHistorySuite.report.format setting and no panel format control (#545), so the multi-file html report type cannot be reintroduced for newly generated reports (no regression of VHS-REQ-640). With nothing configured the generated invocation is identical to the prior hardcoded single-file HTML compare-everything behavior. The settings render in the native Settings editor with no scripted webview and the comparison-report panel keeps scripts disabled (no regression of VHS-REQ-626). The Runtime & Report Settings panel (openRuntimeReportPanelCommand with the runtimeReportPanel renderer) surfaces these flags as Include checkboxes (checked = include the difference class); applyComparisonReportOptionSelection persists each edit to viHistorySuite.report.* with the Include-to-ignore inversion so unchecking a class writes ignore=true.

Title: LabVIEW Container Image Tag Model
Notes: Pure parser/formatter/comparator for nationalinstruments/labview <year>q<quarter>[patch<n>]-<platform> tags; namespace-pinned and newest-first ordered with a higher patch newer and the base release oldest within its group; performs no I/O.

Title: Published Container Image Tag Discovery
Notes: Anonymous read-only bounded Docker Hub tag discovery filtered to platform and the supported year floor through the VHS-REQ-646 model behind an injected fetch boundary with a bounded HTTPS default; failure degrades to empty plus a non-fatal note and never throws.

Title: Local Container Image Tag Discovery
Notes: Enumerates locally pulled nationalinstruments/labview images via an injected docker images boundary and merges with published results marking local presence and registry publication; offline-safe and empty when the Docker CLI is absent.

Title: Container Image Version Selection Setting And Quick-Pick
Notes: Contributes the trust-restricted viHistorySuite.container.imageVersion setting and the labviewViHistory.pickContainerImageVersion command listing discovered versions newest-first with pulled-locally vs available-to-pull annotations and persisting the chosen tag at Global scope; trusted-workspace gated with a Clear option and an actionable empty-discovery message.

Title: Selected Container Version Drives Both Providers With Fail-Closed Resolution
Notes: The locator resolves the selected container image version to a concrete reference for both windows-container and linux-container providers with an explicit full-string override still taking precedence and bypasses the legacy docker-provider-labview-version-not-implemented year pin when a version is selected; unset preserves the prior platform default and a selected-but-unacquirable image fails closed through the existing container-image acquisition path. A selected version whose platform conflicts with the active Docker container host mode fails closed with the classified container-image-platform-mismatch blocked reason instead of silently substituting the platform default. The mismatch compare-time block surfaces a concise toast naming the selected image container platform vs the active Docker engine mode (no provider/rejected-provider internals and no host-native clause) with a Pick Image Version action and suppresses the auto-opened report while still persisting the packet (#532). The image-version picker surfaces a stale cross-platform selection as a leading warning Clear row. The mismatch remediation is delivered through the toast action and the labviewViHistory.pickContainerImageVersion command; the minimized History panel no longer renders an in-panel Pick Image Version CTA or compare-preflight section.

Title: Chain Container Image Version Pick After Docker Provider Selection
Notes: The Runtime & Report Settings panel co-locates the LabVIEW container image version selector with the runtime provider selection: the container section (openRuntimeReportPanelCommand with the runtimeReportPanel renderer) is shown when Docker is the selected or available provider so choosing Docker surfaces the image-version control inline instead of chaining a separate quick-pick. selectContainerVersion persists the chosen tag or clears to the newest supported default in viHistorySuite.container.imageVersion via applyContainerImageVersionSelection; discovery reuses the published and local image catalog boundaries behind injected fetch and list seams. The standalone labviewViHistory.pickContainerImageVersion command stays registered for the compare-preflight remediation CTAs but is removed from the Command Palette.

Title: Live Container Image Pull Progress
Notes: acquireWindowsContainerImage drives the LabVIEW image cold-pull through the Docker Engine API POST /images/create stream over the local daemon socket (Windows named pipe or Linux /var/run/docker.sock) and aggregates per-layer progressDetail.current/total byte counts into a monotonic clamped 0-100 percent with downloaded/total byte figures surfaced in the acquisition progress message. The Engine API path is attempted only where the daemon socket is directly reachable (native Windows or Linux-native); the Linux-to-Windows-docker WSL bridge and any other host fall back to the prior docker pull CLI acquisition so behavior is never worse. An unreachable socket transparently falls back to the CLI; an in-band pull error or non-2xx daemon response is a failed acquisition carrying the error. Read-only anonymous pull of the namespace-pinned nationalinstruments/labview repository with no registry credential header and no new dependency (Node http.request over the socket). Parser and aggregator are pure; the daemon-socket request is behind an injected boundary so the feature is unit-testable on Linux.

Title: Stable Byte-Percentage Pull Progress
Notes: Before the cold-pull begins the extension resolves the image total compressed download size from the Docker Hub registry manifest (anonymous pull token from auth.docker.io then the manifest from registry-1.docker.io; a manifest list or OCI image index is resolved to the windows/amd64 manifest) and sums the per-layer compressed sizes. The pull-progress aggregator divides downloaded bytes by that stable total instead of the partially-known live-stream totals, crediting cached Already exists layers from a per-layer size map so a partial cache still reaches the total; the percent stays monotonic and capped below 100 and the toast shows downloaded over total bytes (for example 42% (8.1 GB / 19.3 GB)). When the stable total is unavailable (non-Docker-Hub registry, auth or network or parse error, timeout, or missing platform) progress falls back to the layer-weighted figure of VHS-REQ-654 so behavior is never worse. Resolution is anonymous with no credentials, bounded by a per-request timeout and a response-size cap, and contacts only the fixed Docker Hub registry and token hosts derived from the image reference so there is no SSRF surface. The reference, challenge, and manifest helpers are pure and the HTTP request is behind an injected boundary so the resolver is unit-testable on Linux without network.

Title: Container Image Pull Phase Signaling
Notes: The pull-progress parser distinguishes the per-layer lifecycle states Downloading, Download complete, Extracting, Pull complete, and Already exists, and the aggregator derives an overall phase (preparing then downloading then extracting then complete) plus a layer-weighted extraction percentage. The acquisition message names the current phase: a pulling message with the download percentage while downloading, an extracting message with its own percentage and completed over total layer count while extracting (for example Extracting container image: image 60% (8/13 layers)), and a finalizing message once every layer is pulled before the existing Container image ready signal. The progress bar advances monotonically through both phases (download owns the larger share and extraction the remainder) so it does not freeze at the download ceiling during the multi-minute unpack. Extraction signaling is robust when the daemon omits Extracting byte detail because the extraction percentage still advances as layers reach Pull complete. The download-phase behavior of VHS-REQ-654 and VHS-REQ-655 is unchanged.
